title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Gravitation — 2020
origin: curated NEB-pattern set filling the 2020 gap for class-11 gravitation

questions.question: Define gravitational field intensity and gravitational potential. Derive the potential $V = -GM/r$ due to a point mass $M$ at distance $r$.
questions.solution:
Field intensity is the force per unit mass ($I = F/m$); potential is the work per unit mass to bring a test mass from infinity ($V = W/m$, zero at infinity).
Force on $m$ at distance $x$: $F = GMm/x^2$ toward $M$. Work bringing $m$ from infinity to $r$: $W = \int_{\infty}^{r} (-GMm/x^2)\,dx$ (negative because displacement opposes the field direction taken positive outward) $= GMm/r \cdot (-1)$… evaluating: $[-GMm/x]_{\infty}^{r} = -GMm/r$. Hence $V = W/m = -GM/r$. The negative sign means the field is attractive — work must be done by an external agent to pull a mass out.

questions.question: What is orbital velocity? Derive $v_o = \sqrt{GM/r}$ for a satellite at height $h$ above Earth (radius $R$), and find its value for a low orbit ($h \approx 0$). ($GM = gR^2$, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$, $R = 6400\,\mathrm{km}$)
questions.solution:
Orbital velocity is the speed needed for a satellite's gravity to supply exactly the centripetal force: $mv_o^2/r = GMm/r^2$, giving $v_o = \sqrt{GM/r}$ with $r = R + h$.
For a low orbit $r \approx R$: $v_o = \sqrt{gR} = \sqrt{10 \times 6.4\times10^6} = \sqrt{64\times10^6} = 8000\,\mathrm{m/s} = 8\,\mathrm{km/s}$ — the first cosmic velocity.

questions.question: If Earth suddenly shrank to half its radius with the same mass, what would happen to $g$ on the surface?
questions.solution: $g = GM/R^2$. Halving $R$ divides by $(1/2)^2 = 1/4$, so $g$ becomes four times: about $40\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$. (Weight would quadruple — shrinking concentrates the same mass closer to you.)
